response: Yes, the SYNTAX score can predict in-hospital outcomes in patients with ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The SYNTAX score is a tool used to assess the complexity of coronary artery disease, and higher scores have been associated with worse in-hospital outcomes, including increased mortality, morbidity, and complications, in patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI.
